items.title_en: Extinct tiger head found under bed after ‘only one in existence’ sold for thousands
items.title_zh: “仅存一个”虎头售价数千美元后，在床底下发现了已灭绝的虎头
items.summary_en: The tiger head is worth a lot of money (Picture: Tom Wren / SWNS) A rare extinct tiger head has been found under a bed weeks after the ‘only one in existence’ sold for a staggering £60,000. The taxidermy head of a Thylacine – also known as a Tasmanian Tiger – was found by a couple in their home, who initially had no idea how rare their discovery really was. They came forward after the only other known surviving taxidermy of its kind was sold at auction back in August, under the mistaken belief it was a fox head.…
items.summary_zh: 虎头价值不菲（图片来源：Tom Wren / SWNS）在“仅存的虎头”以 6 万英镑的惊人价格售出几周后，人们在床下发现了一个罕见的灭绝虎头。一对夫妇在家中发现了袋狼（也称为塔斯马尼亚虎）的标本头，他们最初并不知道他们的发现到底有多罕见。在另一件已知的同类动物标本在八月份的拍卖会上出售后，他们挺身而出。

items.title_en: How Charles Van Doren’s Winning Streak On Twenty-One Almost Brought Down The Quiz Show Industry
items.title_zh: 查尔斯·范·多伦 (Charles Van Doren) 在《二十一》中的连胜几乎摧毁了智力问答节目行业
items.summary_en: NBC/Contributor via Getty Images Charles Van Doren won $129,000 during a 14-week winning streak on the quiz show Twenty-One in the 1950s. “I was involved, deeply involved, in a deception.” That’s what Charles Van Doren told U.S. Congress in 1959. Just two years earlier, Van Doren had appeared on the cover of magazines and was beloved by the American public for his astounding winning streak on the television quiz show Twenty-One .
items.summary_zh: NBC/撰稿人来自 Getty Images 查尔斯·范·多伦 (Charles Van Doren) 在 1950 年代的智力问答节目“二十一”中连续 14 周获胜，赢得了 129,000 美元。 “我深深地卷入了一场欺骗之中。”这就是查尔斯·范·多伦 (Charles Van Doren) 1959 年对美国国会所说的话。就在两年前，范·多伦 (Van Doren) 还登上了杂志封面，并因在电视智力竞赛节目《二十一》中取得惊人的连胜而受到美国公众的喜爱。
